C0.quote: we study the problem of aggregating rankings into a collective ranking
C0.note: The paper studies a social preference function that aggregates weighted rankings. The applications include criteria and votes, and the analysis uses standard voting axioms.

C1.quote: we give an axiomatic characterization of the Squared Kemeny rule
C1.note: AX: characterization (Thm 3.2). AL: NP-completeness and approximation (Sec 5). SB: strategyproofness is violated (Prop 3.4). WD: proportionality and distance guarantees (Sec 4). SI: synthetic samples (Sec 6.2-6.3). EM: city data and Preflib data (Sec 6.1-6.2).

C2.2.quote: A ranking ≻ is a complete, transitive, and anti-symmetric binary relation
C2.2.note: The rankings in a profile carry rational weights.

C2.3.quote: disutility that the outcome ranking ▷ would give to a voter
C2.3.note: The paper refers to 'a voter with a preference order ≻'. In the strategyproofness definition, the true ranking is distinguished from the reported one.

C2.4.quote: agents should never be better off by lying than by voting truthfully
C2.4.note: The text says that the submitted ranking may differ from the held one. There is no separate notation outside the strategyproofness definition.

C3.1.quote: The Squared Kemeny rule satisfies efficiency and participation but violates strategyproofness.
C3.1.note: Only the strategyproofness analysis considers misreporting.

C3.2.note: Section 2 says the weights may 'represent the fraction of voters who report a ranking'. It does not state that the reports are sincere.

C4.1.quote: we use the swap distance between the input ranking and the output rankings
C4.1.note: Disutility and satisfaction are defined through the swap distance between the voter's ranking and the output ranking.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: We now provide a bound on the average satisfaction of any group.
C5.1.note: The criteria in results are Pareto efficiency (Prop 3.4) and group satisfaction or proportionality guarantees (Thm 4.2, Sec 6.3).

C5.2.quote: We can think of 𝑆 as a group of voters
C5.2.note: Satisfaction is measured on the input rankings. No statement relates these rankings to held attitudes.

VOT.quote_behav: agents should never be better off by lying than by voting truthfully
VOT.note: Voters are strategic only in the strategyproofness analysis. In all other analyses, inputs are taken as given.

C8.1.quote: We hence say an SPF 𝑓 is strategyproof if there are no profiles

C8.2.quote: As the last axiom of this section, we will consider strategyproofness.

claims.quote: the Squared Kemeny rule has the potential of providing a consensus ranking
Proportionality may be desirable in this context to ensure that
the Squared Kemeny rule caters to all group sizes

C9.1.note: These are claims about which rule should be used and about fairness to groups of voters.

C9.2.note: In multi-agent settings, the claims about satisfying voter groups and reflecting their interests need submitted rankings to equal voters' true preferences. This is not stated. The link from swap distance to satisfaction is stated.
